chunks: ʿAlī, from his father, from al-Nawfalī, from al-Sakūnī, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام used to say: Do not bare your teeth openly while you have committed disgraceful deeds, and the one who has committed evil deeds should not feel secure from a night assault.

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Amīr al-Muʾminīn, Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام
key_terms.الْأَعْمَالَ الْفَاضِحَةَ: disgraceful deeds that expose a person to shame
key_terms.الْبَيَاتَ: a sudden night assault or unexpected calamity
key_terms.وَاضِحَةٍ: the visible teeth; used here for openly smiling or showing cheer

ai.seo_question: Why should a sinner not feel secure after committing evil deeds?
ai.summary: This narration warns against false ease, shamelessness, and feeling secure after committing sins. It teaches that evil actions expose a person to disgrace and to sudden divine requital, so one should live with moral caution and repentance.

en.hubeali: Ali, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘Amir Al-Momineenasws was saying: ‘You should not show (your teeth) clearly and you have done the shameful deed, nor should he sleep securely, the one who committed the sins’.
en.sarwar: 5. Ali has narrated from his father from al-Nawfali from al-Sakuni from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “

Amir al-Mu’minin, Ali ibn abu Talib (a.s.) has said, ‘You must never show your teeth (smile) when you have committed disgraceful deeds and never feel safe from misfortune to strike you due to (your) sinful deeds.’”
